data.name: Monitor_Name
data.value: Adaptive Agent for PHD2 — Sky Conditions

data.name: Monitor_Description
data.value:
Continuously measures observing conditions and reports them to N.I.N.A. as a safety device. (It appears under the “Safety Monitor” category: that is N.I.N.A.'s name for the slot, not this monitor's role.)
The guide camera judges the sky, both to pause the sequence and to let it resume: the guide star sits in the same telescope as the imaging camera and is measured every few seconds, even while the sequence is paused. It needs Adaptive Agent 3.1 or later: with an older Agent clouds are not judged, and a warning says so.
It reports UNSAFE on: a star lost for a long time; a guide-star signal below half of its clear-sky level (after about 3.5 minutes with the factory settings: clouds, or a guide-camera fault); a guide channel gone silent while guiding was expected; the Agent unreachable during an active session. It returns SAFE when the guide star stays above 80% of its clear-sky level for a minute and is tracked steadily: about 2 minutes after the sky clears. If the guide star or the guide exposure changed during unsafe, the clear sky must last 5 minutes (Adaptive Agent 3.2 or later): from the SNR alone, a brighter star under the cloud would look like clear sky. The return after a lost star, a lost Agent or a silent guide channel goes through the same confirmation. During calibration, the Guiding Assistant and autofocus (when N.I.N.A. stops guiding for it) the sky verdict is suspended; a lost star, however, still counts. The imaging camera measures the sky on every frame, for information only.
ADVANCED SEQUENCER — recommended setup: Trigger On Unsafe └ Before Waiting For Safety └ Recovery probe (Adaptive Agent)
The instruction takes no exposures: it keeps guiding alive. If guiding stops while waiting, if the star stays lost for long, or if unsafe lasts beyond the restart interval, it restarts guiding; it ends on its own when the monitor returns SAFE. Do not put instructions that stop guiding or park (Park, Find Home, Stop Guiding) in the unsafe branch. Put the Trigger On Unsafe in the target container, not at the sequence root.
The monitor only reports: N.I.N.A.'s Sequence Engine stays in charge of the sequence, your end-of-sequence criteria always win, and any running recovery is cancelled the moment the sequence ends.

data.name: Probe_MinInterval_Tip
data.value: Minimum interval between two guiding restarts, and also how long guiding must have stopped, or the star been lost, before it is restarted. Never below 1 minute. Factory value 5.

data.name: Probe_Timeout_Tip
data.value: After how many minutes of continued unsafe, with guiding running, the probe restarts the guide channel, and again every as many minutes while unsafe lasts (on 3/10 a guide-camera fault cleared exactly at a guiding restart). Postponed while the guide is confirming a clear sky (Adaptive Agent 3.2 or later): a restart would reset the confirmation. Factory value 12.

data.name: Settings_AgentLost_Check
data.value: Report unsafe if the Agent becomes unreachable during an active session

data.name: Settings_AgentLost_Help
data.value: Losing the Agent means losing observation of both sky and guiding — a risk condition. The monitor stays connected in N.I.N.A. and, if the Agent does not answer for several checks in a row, reports unsafe: it never goes safe just because it lost contact. With guiding intentionally stopped, an offline Agent raises no alarm. When the Agent returns, with cloud safety on the monitor goes safe only after the guide has confirmed a clear sky.

data.name: Settings_Cloud_Check

data.name: Settings_Cloud_Help
data.value: The monitor reports unsafe when the guide-star signal stays below half of its clear-sky level (about 3.5 minutes with the factory settings) and returns safe when it is back above 80% for a minute, with the star tracked steadily (5 minutes if the guide star or the guide exposure changed during unsafe). When disabled, no cloud leads to unsafe: only a lost star, a silent guide channel and a lost Agent remain. Requires Adaptive Agent 3.1 or later with its sky sensor on: otherwise clouds are not judged and a warning says so. The imaging camera never reports unsafe: it measures the sky for information only.

data.name: Settings_GuideObs_Check
data.value: Report unsafe when the guide channel goes silent

data.name: Settings_GuideObs_Help
data.value: Watches whether PHD2 is still delivering guide frames at all — not how good the guiding is (that is the adaptive engine's job). Legitimate pauses (meridian flip, autofocus, manual stop) are announced by PHD2 and never raise an alarm; a guide camera that dies stops talking instead, and that silence is what this detects. A severe PHD2 alert or a burst of per-frame star errors halves the delay. When frames return, with cloud safety on the monitor goes safe only after the guide has confirmed a clear sky.

data.name: Settings_GuidePolls
data.value: Silent → unsafe (polls):

data.name: Settings_GuidePolls_Tip
data.value: Polls of confirmed silence before declaring UNSAFE. Frames flowing again drain the count. Higher = more tolerant of brief gaps. Factory value 3: at 15 s unsafe comes about 2 minutes after the last frame.

data.name: Settings_GuideSilence
data.value: Silence threshold (s):

data.name: Settings_GuideSilence_Tip
data.value: Seconds without ANY guide frame (guiding or re-acquisition attempts) before the channel is considered suspect. Halved when corroborated by a severe PHD2 alert or repeated per-frame star errors. Factory value 90 (allowed 20–600).

data.name: Settings_Meridian_Label
data.value: Meridian protection

data.name: Settings_Meridian_Check
data.value: Authorize the mechanical meridian flip during a long unsafe hold

data.name: Settings_Meridian_Help
data.value: Without this, NINA reacts to an unsafe flip deadline by stopping mount tracking — and nothing ever restarts it: the guide star drifts away, frames trail, and the monitor loses every eye it decides with. The night ends there even if the sky clears (verified on 19/7). This window reports safe so the flip can run, and protects it to the end (recenter and guiding resumed included), then restores the unsafe hold: it protects the monitor's own ability to keep observing, it never judges the sky. Reconsider only if other devices (roof, dome) start consuming this monitor's safe state.

data.name: Settings_MeridianLead
data.value: Open window (min before flip deadline):

data.name: Settings_MeridianLead_Tip
data.value: How many minutes before the flip deadline (meridian + your NINA 'max minutes after meridian') the window opens. Arriving early lets the flip run through NINA's normal path before the tracking-stop guard fires. Factory value 4 (allowed 1–10).

data.name: Settings_SkyDegrade_Polls
data.value: Clouds → unsafe (polls):

data.name: Settings_Tip_SkyDegradePolls
data.value: How long the guide-star signal must stay collapsed before UNSAFE, after the 90 s the Agent needs to confirm it. With the factory settings: 8 polls × 15 s = 2 minutes, about 3.5 minutes in total. Higher = more tolerant of short clouds.

data.name: Settings_Interval_Help
data.value: How often the plugin asks the Agent how things are going. Each check is a “poll”: the poll values further down are counted in these checks (at 15 s, 8 polls = 2 minutes), so changing this interval changes those times too. Allowed range: 5–120, factory value 15.

data.name: Settings_ManageExt_Check
data.value: Also manage an Agent not started by the plugin

data.name: Settings_ManageExt_Help
data.value: On (default): when NINA closes, the plugin gracefully shuts down any reachable Agent — even one it did not start — so PHD2 always gets its starting parameters back. Turn it off if you run the Agent standalone and want it to outlive NINA. Note: for an external Agent there is no process handle — if it hangs, only the Agent's own orphan recovery cleans up at next start.

data.name: Settings_Recovery_Body
data.value: That single instruction is the complete recovery loop. It takes no exposures: it waits for SAFE, which comes when the guide star confirms a clear sky, and if guiding stops or the star stays lost meanwhile it restarts guiding. Do not put instructions that stop guiding or park (Park, Find Home, Stop Guiding) in the unsafe branch: they would blind the only judge. Put the Trigger On Unsafe in the target container, not at the sequence root: that way the end area (park, cover) still runs at the end of the night. No extra containers or Camera instructions are needed.

data.name: Settings_Recovery_Intro
data.value: To let the session resume by itself after clouds, add ONE instruction to your Advanced Sequence:

data.name: Settings_Recovery_Title
data.value: Automatic recovery — sequence setup

data.name: Settings_SavedAuto
data.value: Settings are saved automatically.

data.name: Settings_StarLost_Help
data.value: How long the guide star must stay lost before the monitor reports unsafe. Default 5 minutes (300). Allowed range: 30–1800. Higher values reduce false positives at the cost of slower detection; lower values risk triggering on short losses PHD2 would have recovered. The lost star is measured on PHD2's events and, once the star is found again, with cloud safety on the monitor goes safe only after the guide has confirmed a clear sky.

data.value: Telemetry forwarding enabled

data.name: Settings_Telemetry_Help
data.value: On every saved exposure, sends HFR, star count and image statistics to the Agent (HTTP POST), shown in the dashboard. Information only: it never decides safe or unsafe. Optional: if the Agent is offline nothing happens and NINA is never disturbed. Disable to send no data.

data.name: Settings_Telemetry_Label
data.value: Forward NINA per-exposure metrics to the Agent

data.name: Settings_Tip_AgentLostPolls
data.value: Polls with the Agent unreachable before declaring UNSAFE. Escalates only during an active session — with guiding intentionally stopped, an offline Agent raises no alarm. Factory value 4: at 15 s that is 1 minute.

data.name: Settings_Tip_ClearPolls
data.value: Polls of guide-confirmed clear sky needed to fully drain the cloud accumulator and return SAFE. Clear sky only counts once the Agent has confirmed it (one minute, five if the guide star or exposure changed during unsafe) and while the star is tracked steadily; it also governs the return after a lost star, a lost Agent and a silent guide channel. Higher = slower, more cautious return to safe. Factory value 4: at 15 s that is 1 minute, after the Agent's confirmation.
